title: Crumple
description: A real film photo print, Kodak's sun hats on a wall, lying on the table, animated like stop-motion at 5 frames a second. Each press crushes it one step further in about a second: the first squeeze breaks it into sharp creases and flat facets, each later one folds it tighter until it is a faceted ball under the lamp. Keep pressing and it opens back out a step at a time, keeping every crease.
intent: Realistic paper in discrete stages, shown at a stepped stop-motion frame rate: the crease simulation is baked offline, and each press is keyed as five held 200ms frames (crush, crush, overshoot, relax, settle), the first drawn on the press itself, so every step lands and settles in about one second.
sources: Print photo: kodim03 (hats), a 35mm film scan from Kodak Photo CD PCD0992, released by the Eastman Kodak Company for unrestricted usage; via https://github.com/MohamedBakrAli/Kodak-Lossless-True-Color-Image-Suite (mirror of http://r0k.us/graphics/kodak/), cropped square and re-encoded as webp.
